correctness.rationale: Both discrepancy bounds are correct. The two-dimensional Erdős-Turán-Koksma inequality plus the degree-4 Weil bound gives O(p^{-1/2}(log p)^2) after choosing H about sqrt(p); the m2=0 frequencies contribute only O(log p/p). For the lower bound, taking the full first-coordinate interval reduces to the one-dimensional second-coordinate discrepancy, and Koksma applied to e(x) yields D* >= |T|/(2 pi (p-1)). For p=5 mod 24, quartic-character decomposition gives T1=g(chi)+g(phi)+g(chibar), with g(phi)=sqrt(p) and chi(-1)=-1, so the two quartic Gauss sums have purely imaginary sum and Re(T1)=sqrt(p). Hence |T1-1| >= sqrt(p)-1 and the stated c p^{-1/2} bound follows for all sufficiently large primes in that progression.

originality.rationale: The proof is a textbook Fourier-discrepancy template: Weil controls every nontrivial two-dimensional frequency, and one explicitly large one-dimensional Fourier coefficient supplies the lower bound. The quartic-character identity at p=5 mod 24 is a standard Gauss-sum evaluation. Specializing these standard ingredients to h^4 does not establish a new discrepancy method or a new finite-field exponential-sum theorem.

scientific_value.rationale: The result gives a clean worked benchmark, but leaves a logarithmic gap and concerns one elementary monomial point set. With no new technique, optimized exponent, or broader family theorem, the scientific contribution is too limited for validation as an independent research finding.
